Hussein was the king of Jordan from 1952 to 1999. Coming to the throne at seventeen, he steered a small, poor country through wars, coups and the arrival of hundreds of thousands of refugees.

He was beside his grandfather, King Abdullah, when Abdullah was shot in Jerusalem in 1951. He lost the West Bank and East Jerusalem to Israel in the Six-Day War of 1967. In Black September 1970 his army drove the Palestinian armed groups out of Jordan. He kept secret contacts with Israel for decades.

In 1994 he signed the peace treaty with Israel. He was popular at home and respected abroad as a moderate. His son Abdullah II succeeded him. See also Palestinians in Jordan.
sum: Hussein was the king of Jordan from 1952 to 1999. Coming to the throne at seventeen, he steered a small, poor country through wars, coups and the arrival of hundreds of thousands of refugees.
